quarterly_data.signal: Fiscal Q3 revenue rose 36.2% sequentially and 123% year over year, again above guidance, as K&S ramped flexible production capacity aggressively. GAAP gross margin was 47.8%, GAAP EPS $1.07 and non-GAAP EPS $1.20. Total operating expenses were $89.7 million GAAP and $82.6 million non-GAAP, the sequential increase largely from variable incentive compensation accruals plus some added fixed resources. Tax expense was $15.3 million with the effective rate expected to remain slightly above 20%. By end market: general semiconductor revenue rose 52.6% sequentially to $227.2 million, memory rose 8.8% to $34.0 million, and automotive and industrial rose 9% to $24.2 million; aftermarket products and services also rose on higher installed-base production.
quarterly_data.figure: Q3 revenue +36.2% QoQ and +123% YoY; gross margin 47.8%; non-GAAP EPS $1.20; general semi $227.2M (+52.6% QoQ), memory $34.0M, auto/industrial $24.2M

quarterly_data.signal: Fiscal Q4 (September quarter) guidance: revenue up 13.5% sequentially to $375 MILLION with gross margin of 48%. Non-GAAP operating expenses rise temporarily to approximately $87.5 million on the quarterly accrual of the performance-linked variable incentive compensation plan. GAAP EPS is guided to $1.29 and non-GAAP EPS to $1.42. Management said it continues to anticipate ABOVE-AVERAGE DEMAND IN FISCAL 2027.
quarterly_data.figure: Q4 FY2026 guide $375M (+13.5% QoQ); gross margin 48%; GAAP EPS $1.29, non-GAAP EPS $1.42

quarterly_data.signal: Demand indicators are unusually strong for K&S: utilisation rates improved sequentially in ALL regions and ALL end markets, with China utilisation over 95% and both memory and general semiconductor end markets around 90%. Management is seeing inbound purchase orders extending into fiscal Q2 - explicitly noting 'usually, that doesn't happen for us; we usually don't have purchase orders that go out that far' - and customers in China continuing to build factories. On that basis management is confident the traditional business stays strong through the FIRST HALF OF FISCAL 2027, with more colour on the second half promised on the November call. Management declined to project a return to the $1.5 billion annual levels of 2021-2022, calling those pandemic-driven extremes a very high bar.
quarterly_data.figure: China utilisation >95%; memory and general semi end markets ~90%; purchase orders extending into fiscal Q2

quarterly_data.signal: Advanced Solutions, which includes the Fluxless Thermo-Compression (FTC) bonding platform, recognised revenue 20% ABOVE last quarter's record. K&S is maintaining its target of OVER $100 MILLION in Advanced Solutions revenue for fiscal 2026, and for fiscal 2027 Lester Wong guided TCB revenue to a range of $150 MILLION TO $200 MILLION - significant sequential growth. The company remains closely engaged with a broad base of IDM, OSAT and foundry customers as heterogeneous packaging goes mainstream, with particular confidence in heterogeneous integration around logic for Fluxless TCB.
quarterly_data.figure: Advanced Solutions revenue 20% above prior record; >$100M Advanced Solutions target for FY2026; TCB guided to $150M-$200M in FY2027

quarterly_data.signal: Beyond thermocompression, K&S accelerated its HYBRID BONDING program over the last year and says its hybrid bonder has unique features not currently in the market; it PLANS TO DELIVER A HYBRID BONDING TOOL TO A CUSTOMER IN THE FIRST HALF OF FISCAL 2027. It is also investing significantly in a PANEL-level project, seeing a lot of interest from IDMs, foundries and OSATs because panel geometry allows many more dies on a rectangle than a circle; specific panel applications are still being scoped with customers. Management frames FTC, vertical wire, direct copper-to-copper, hybrid and panel-based architectures as the emerging packaging set that will be critically necessary across a much wider array of semiconductor production, and stresses the industry is still in the relatively early stages of this More-than-Moore advanced packaging transition.
quarterly_data.figure: Hybrid bonding tool to be delivered to a customer in H1 FY2027

quarterly_data.signal: Capacity: the Singapore capital expansion is progressing well and remains on track for completion by the FIRST FISCAL HALF OF 2027, supporting Advanced Solutions growth over coming years. For the traditional wire bonding business, K&S has increased capacity FOURFOLD compared with about two quarters ago through its flexible manufacturing model. Management said it is explicitly focused on not losing market share because of capacity constraints, noted K&S has supported $400 million quarters before, and did not see a $450 million quarterly run rate at this point while committing to ramp further if needed.
quarterly_data.figure: Wire bonding capacity increased fourfold versus ~two quarters ago; Singapore expansion completing in H1 fiscal 2027

quarterly_data.signal: K&S made a notable structural claim about wire bonding in AI infrastructure: it estimates the DATA CENTER MARKET RELIES ON WIRE BONDING TECHNOLOGY AT LEAST AS MUCH AS, IF NOT MORE THAN, traditional semiconductor markets such as smartphones and PCs, because the majority of data center chips are still traditionally wire bonded - general infrastructure, networking, communication, power management and storage. Ball bonding is the more prevalent technology for data center power management, while wedge bonding remains more focused on automotive and high-current applications. Data center expansion therefore drives demand for BOTH the thermocompression and the wire bonding lines.

Memory: shipments rose 8.8% sequentially to $34 million after strong growth the prior quarter, currently focused on delivering NAND technology and capacity. Management stated that DATA CENTER IS NOW THE LARGEST END APPLICATION ACROSS GLOBAL NAND PRODUCTION, with about 40% of the NAND market going to data centers. Beyond NAND, the vertical wire team continues to work closely with memory customers as they develop NEW FORMS OF STACKED DRAM applications.
quarterly_data.figure: Memory $34M (+8.8% QoQ); ~40% of the NAND market goes to data centers

quarterly_data.signal: Automotive and industrial demand improved 9% sequentially to $24.2 million after strong improvement the prior quarter, with robust demand for high I/O and high-volume power and mixed-signal packaging plus increased demand for high-current WEDGE solutions. The wedge bonding suite is a critical part of the automotive and industrial offering, a market that has faced industry-level headwinds for several years; K&S expanded the portfolio through that period and expects long-term share growth in battery and plug-in hybrids as they drive new power semiconductor technology and capacity requirements. The company also marked its 75th anniversary during the quarter.
